notes: The in of in all those places is given to the object marker standing on that phrase, which rule 16 reads as a marked object the ASV demotes and rule 33's own third limit defers to; the competing reading treats the phrase as a bare adverbial accusative and gives the word to the noun under rule 33, but a marker is written on it here.

סָבַב is recast as the adverbial phrase in circuit, headed on the content word carrying the lexeme (rule 31), and the to that reaches its bare object Beth-el is placed with it under rule 44's supplied-preposition clause and rule 33's direct-object question. The competing reading is rule 33's dissolved-verb paragraph, which would give the to to the toponym as the word stating what the recast phrase contributes; I took the direct-object reading because Beth-el is what סָבַב governs in the Hebrew.
In כָּל־הַמְּקוֹמוֹת הָאֵלֶּה the phrase's one determiner is the those the demonstrative licenses, so both articles are unrepresented (rules 41, 47).
